i193.title: Vendor the official nand2tetris vectors (projects 1–5) from web-ide via a sync script; confirm the licence that covers them

nodes.body:
Foundation plan (#318) item 1.6 pulls this forward as **the held-out oracle**: vendored, pinned, on a protected path — tests no implementer may edit.

What the testing audit measured, so the builder does not redo it: zero `.hdl`/`.tst`/`.cmp` files exist in the repo; the vectors live as TypeScript strings in `src/core/testing/project1{Tst,Cmp}Fixtures.ts` (16 keys each). Compared with `web-ide/projects/src/project_01/*.ts`, comments and whitespace normalised: **15 identical, 0 differ, 0 missing** (`Nand` is HACER's 16th and has no upstream stub). So vendoring Project 1 is a lock, not a change.

Additions to the criteria:
- [ ] ship **Project 1 first**, in its own PR; Projects 2–5 follow in later PRs (the files are data and `conformance/vectors/` is already excluded from the size budget, but one project per PR keeps each reviewable)
- [ ] a test asserts that the 16 hand-transcribed fixtures match the vendored files, so the two cannot drift until #194 retires the transcriptions
- [ ] record the `web-ide` commit the files were taken from
- [ ] this unblocks #204, whose verification command reads `conformance/vectors/01/Xor.*`, and the differential harness (#338)

**Same path problem as #338, same fix.** Criterion 1 says `scripts/sync-vectors.sh` copies from `../web-ide` — a sibling checkout that exists only in the owner's local workspace. Any cloud agent or CI runner clones just `mezivillager/hacer` and would fail on a missing directory.

`web-ide` is public (`https://github.com/nand2tetris/web-ide.git`). Amend the criterion to **clone it at a pinned commit and record that commit in the LICENSE notice** alongside the licence finding. The sync script then works anywhere, and re-running it later reproduces exactly the same vectors instead of whatever the laptop happened to hold.

This also matters for what the issue is *for*: these vectors are a **held-out oracle on a protected path**, and an oracle whose provenance is "a directory on one machine" is weaker than one pinned to a public commit.

i199.title: HDL parser fuzz: never throws uncaught; error spans in range

nodes.body:
**Before anyone picks this up: `fast-check` is not a dependency.** `grep fast-check package.json` returns nothing, and it is absent from the lockfile. The issue's "property:" wording implies it; the library that would provide it arrives with **#198**, which is itself blocked by #385.

This is the same trap #355 hit on 2026-09-23 — its criteria asserted `fast-check` was already available, a builder discovered it was not, and the right answer was **not** to add the dependency. Two precedents now exist in this repo for doing property-style testing without it:
- `src/core/hdl/compiler.test.ts` (#362): an **exhaustive permutation sweep** plus a seeded `mulberry32` sample. Over a small space an exhaustive sweep is a *proof*, not a sample — stronger than property testing, losing only shrinking.
- #398's verifier went further with a **20,000-case differential sweep** against an independently built oracle.

So: do this with hand-rolled grammar mutation and a seeded PRNG, and **do not add `fast-check`** — that decision belongs to #198. Say in the PR which shape you used and what space it covers.

One more thing worth stating, because it is the failure mode here: **a fuzz test that never fails proves nothing about the fuzzer.** Show the generator failing against a deliberately broken parser (a reverted guard, a mutated span calculation) before trusting a green run — #362's first property generator was measured **vacuous**, 0 of 400 cases failing against the unfixed compiler, until the generator itself was fixed.

i403.title: removeJunction deletes valid user-drawn wires on gesture-written documents (trunk and branch share one `from`)

nodes.body:
**Three things measured during #396's re-review that belong in this issue's acceptance criteria.**

1. **A naive option 2 ("delete every listed wire") also deletes a feed wire whose `to` IS the junction.** The re-viewer mutated `removeJunction` to option 2 and measured survivors `[]` on the junction-endpoint test — so option 2 needs a **stated policy for that endpoint**, not just "delete them all". Without it, option 2 trades a gesture-document bug for an imported-document one.
2. **#396's "undisturbed fan-out must not regress" test does not survive option 2 either.** It pins the *current contract*, not an invariant. Name it explicitly in this issue's acceptance: whichever option is chosen must say what happens to that test — updated, replaced, or deliberately broken with a reason.
3. **Reachability is wider than #396's B-009 row first said**: besides `applyJunctionRelocations` (gate/node drag) and the programmatic facade, `busActions.ts:268` — bus-component recalculation — also reaches `removeJunction`. B-009 is corrected; this issue's options should be judged against all three entry points.

The reframing this issue carries is the right one: in gesture documents **every listed wire is complete**, so the defect is a wrong *contract* — "keep one, delete the rest" — rather than a wrong trunk pick. Any option that still picks a survivor is answering the old question.
